Hi Elena / CloudApps team,

Quick heads up: we have a planned maintenance window for the US-Central region the night of Mar 9 (UTC Mar 10). This is a rolling maintenance to refresh kernel modules and validate a new driver compatibility profile across a subset of serving nodes. We expect low impact for most customers but want to make sure your team is aware and coordinated.

High-level details:
- Window: 2027-03-09 23:00 - 2027-03-10 05:00 UTC (rolling, staggered across AZs)
- Scope: kernel module update + node restarts (rolling, single-AZ at a time)
- Expected impact: brief connection re-establishment per node (~30-90s) for active sessions; streaming responses may see short stalls; no data loss expected
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to healthy AZs and rollback plan if errors observed

Requested action from CloudApps:
1) Confirm whether you will be running any critical long-running inference jobs in that window so we can coordinate bypass for those workloads.
2) Share any IP allowlist changes if you require us to pre-authorize additional egress endpoints.

Attachments: maintenance-runbook.pdf (runbook + rollback steps), kernel-compat-matrix.xlsx (models vs driver compatibility notes).

I'll follow up with a final confirmation 48 hours before the window and post a status update to status.redwood.ai during the work. If you want a maintenance-free path, we can schedule a per-customer migration to a pinned capacity for that night (separate conversation).

Thanks,

Hi Elena — thanks for the questions, brief technical summary and recommended mitigations below.

What to expect for long-running jobs:
- Rolling restarts will evict KV caches on affected nodes; active TCP connections will be terminated when the node reboots. Jobs that rely on persistent socket connections can fail unless they have retry/ reconnect logic.

Recommended mitigations:
1) Add exponential backoff and idempotency to any inference job (best practice regardless).
2) For jobs that cannot tolerate reconnects, consider scheduling them outside the 23:00-05:00 UTC window.
3) If neither option is feasible, we can provision a pinned Dedicated pool for CloudApps for that single night — contact Nikhil and we’ll quote temporary capacity.

Operational notes:
- We are staging the updates across AZs in this order: usc-a -> usc-b -> usc-c. Each AZ will be drained and verified before proceeding (~45–90 minutes per AZ depending on verification checks).
- Runbook and rollback: see attached maintenance-runbook.pdf. Kernel compatibility matrix in kernel-compat-matrix.xlsx — models with known sensitivity to the new driver are highlighted.
- We'll send a 48h reminder and a 2h pre-work notice via status.redwood.ai; a live incident page will be created during the window.

If useful, ops@cloudapps.com and I can set a 15-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the runbook.

—Marissa
